findings.how_to_check: In Stata, create a test dataset with `fs_namefrst=""`, `fs_namelast="smith"`, and `sex=1`, and run `abeclean fs_namefrst fs_namelast, sex(sex) initial(mi_fs) nicknames nonysiis`. Stata will halt with `no observations r(2000)`. Repeat with `fs_namefrst="."` and `fs_namelast="smith"` to confirm that punctuation-only strings similarly produce r(2000).
findings.suggested_fix:
Clean each name component independently conditional on that specific component containing cleanable alphabetic characters, e.g.:
gen fs_namefrst_cleaned = ""
gen fs_namelast_cleaned = ""
gen mi_fs = ""
quietly count if ustrregexm(fs_namefrst, "[a-zA-Z]")
if r(N) > 0 abeclean fs_namefrst, sex(sex) initial(mi_fs) nicknames nonysiis
quietly count if ustrregexm(fs_namelast, "[a-zA-Z]")
if r(N) > 0 abeclean fs_namelast, sex(sex) nicknames nonysiis
Alternatively, update abeclean.ado so that split is guarded against empty variables.
findings.title: abeclean is still called and crashes with r(2000) when only one name field is populated or when a field lacks alphabetic characters
findings.what_the_code_does: The guard checks `quietly count if fs_namefrst!="" | fs_namelast!=""` and calls `abeclean fs_namefrst fs_namelast, ...` whenever `r(N) > 0`. However, inside `abeclean.ado`, the command iterates over each variable in `varlist` independently (`foreach oldvar of varlist `varlist'`), strips non-alphabetic characters via `ustrregexra(`var', "[^a-z ]", "")`, and executes `split `var', gen(`temp')` without error trapping. If either name field contains all empty strings or only non-alphabetic characters (e.g. punctuation or numbers) across all records in a birthplace file, `split` executes on an entirely empty variable and terminates execution with `r(2000)` ('no observations').
findings.why_it_matters: While the guard succeeds for the placebo run (where both fields are initialized to empty strings), a substantive FamilySearch run over hundreds of birthplace files will halt whenever a birthplace has records with only a first name or only a last name, or where transcription artifacts leave no cleanable letters. Because `1b_fs_divided_files.do` processes birthplace files in a loop, a single failure aborts the entire divided-file preparation stage.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied. Per review protocol, claims-vs-code could not evaluate manuscript claims or linking rates against manuscript text.
External census datasets on drives D: and F: were unavailable, so the exact frequency of birthplace files with unilateral or punctuation-only FamilySearch names could not be empirically measured.
The Stata pipeline could not be executed in this read-only environment; runtime behavior and failure modes were verified by tracing Stata ado-file source code.
The review scope was targeted to uncommitted working tree changes in MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do; unchanged linking scripts were reviewed only as context for inputs and outputs.
structured_output.summary: The uncommitted change in MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do successfully allows the placebo run to bypass `abeclean` when both FamilySearch name fields are empty, preserving Ancestry names. However, the compound OR guard (`fs_namefrst!="" | fs_namelast!=""`) still submits records to `abeclean` when only one name field is populated or when entries contain no alphabetic letters, causing `abeclean`'s internal `split` call to abort execution with `r(2000)`. Guarding each name component independently or handling empty fields inside `abeclean` is required before running the substantive FamilySearch linking pipeline.

verified_clean.evidence: When placebo is active, fs_namefrst and fs_namelast are blank, so lines 68-76 take the else branch, setting fs_namefrst_cleaned="", fs_namelast_cleaned="", and mi_fs=""; the replacement conditions at lines 77-81 are false, leaving Ancestry's f_name, l_name, and mi unchanged.
verified_clean.item: Placebo branch correctly preserves Ancestry names and middle initials without modifications.

verified_clean.evidence: In MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do:46-59, the input birthplace file asserts isid id, merges 1:1 histid with fs_names<yr>.dta with keep(1 3), and explicitly asserts assert _N==`n0' so no master rows are dropped or duplicated.
verified_clean.item: Merge with FamilySearch names validates master record preservation and 1:1 key uniqueness.

verified_clean.evidence: Lines 63-64 confirm the existence of sex and generate byte sex = 1 for the all-male sample, preventing abeclean from halting on missing sex or invalid gender codes.
verified_clean.item: Sex variable initialization ensures abeclean nickname table preconditions are met.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
